collections: Vec / HashMap / Option and More

This page explains how collections and common value types are implemented, and the type method surface that Sla code can use directly. Collections are not extern functions, but SA macros + layout contracts (.sal); Sla method calls are lowered by the sla_std/std_surface.sla_meta rules to the corresponding macros.

Layout Contracts (.sal)

ConstantMeaning
Vec_SIZE = 24Size of the Vec struct; fields ptr = +0, cap = +8, len = +16 (alloc/vec.sal)
HashMap_SIZE = 40Fields slots/cap/len/tombs/seed at +0/+8/+16/+24/+32
HashMapSlot_SIZE = 32A slot contains hash/key/value/state; states are EMPTY/FILLED/TOMB

Sla Method Surface (std_surface.sla_meta)

TypeAvailable members
VecAssociated new; push, len(), index reading/writing v[i], fallible remove(index)
HashSetAssociated new; insert, contains, len()
BTreeSetAssociated new; insert, contains, len()
BoxAssociated new / into_raw / from_raw; methods get, as_ptr
Rc / ArcAssociated new / clone; methods get, as_ptr
Cell / RefCellAssociated new; Cell has get / set
OptionSome(v) / None; is_some, is_none, get, unwrap, unwrap_or
ResultOk(v) / Err(e); is_ok, is_err, unwrap, unwrap_or
SliceIndex reading s[i] and address views

HashMap: Hash Seed and Iteration Order Conventions (TS-11, Written 2026-10-29)

The hash seed is entirely fixed, with no per-process randomization: the default SA-layer HashMap entry point hashes with seed 0 (xor-shift finalization); SLA's Hash trait's DefaultHasher is FNV-1a-shaped (with a fixed seed constant and primes); although a SipHash-shaped RandomState exists, its default key is likewise a compile-time constant, and the map path does not seed from OS entropy. Iteration order is table-slot order, deterministically decided by (hash, capacity, insertion order) — but the contract convention is iteration order is not guaranteed: although the implementation is deterministic, programs must not depend on any specific order. An accompanying factual note: the absence of randomization means there is no hash-flooding protection; whether to handle that is a later security decision and is outside the scope of this section.

A Real Example

From sa_plugin_sla/tests/import_fixtures/std_nested/uses_vec.sla:

@import "sa_std/vec.sa"

fn imported_vec_sum() -> i32 {
    let values: Vec<i32> = Vec::new();
    values.push(2);
    values.push(3);
    return values[0] + values[1];
}

The generic spelling Vec<i32> is monomorphized by the compiler according to the element type (the %elem_size/_TYPED_{elem_ty} variants in the macros come from this).

NoteThe same directory contains more collection implementations usable through .sa macros: binary_heap.sa, btree_map.sa, btree_set.sa, hashmap.sa, hashset.sa, collections/linked_list.sa, vec_deque.sa. These have no dedicated Sla method surface, and need to be used at the SA layer by importing the macros.

Category A: Geometric-Growth Bulk Surface and Pools (2026-11-02)

GAP-BULKAPPEND closed. The native layer adds three geometric-growth primitives (sa_std/alloc/vec.sa), with a growth sequence starting 0→4 and doubling thereafter, in the same sequence as @sa_vec_push (push's 0→1 start has been unified to 0→4 by decision); @sa_vec_reserve keeps its exact one-shot size semantics unchanged, because incremental growth with exact reservation is an O(n²) trap.
PrimitiveSemantics
@sa_vec_reserve_growGeometric reservation: when capacity is insufficient, grow to max(required, doubled); when sufficient, do nothing
@sa_vec_extendAppend a span of memory in bulk (geometric growth + a single memcpy-level copy)
@sa_vec_extend_vecAppend a whole Vec; self-append (source and target are the same buffer) panics loudly
Bulk copying is bound to @sa_mem_copy_nonoverlapping (core/mem.sa, the memcpy surface); the new primitives do not promise to zero-fill [len, cap) (consistent with push's historical behaviour; only reserve/with_capacity zero-fills the whole buffer). On the SLA side, see vec_packed.sla and vec_grow.sla: sa_vec_grow_to, the geometric extend family (including packed variants for u16/i32/f64) and mark/rewind (sa_vec_mark / sa_vec_rewind / sa_vec_rewind_bytes).
Pool and linking pattern libraries (SLA layer): slice_pool.sla, a byte-segment pool (first-fit + splitting + adjacent merging; a mismatched free panics loudly); slot_pool.sla, a fixed-size slot pool (freelist LIFO, double-free panics loudly; deep elements are outside the v1 contract); rel_link.sla, relative-offset linking (u32 offset fields + REL_NIL; offsets still resolve after the whole block is relocated).
